clue.text: A child gets attached to this secrecy

definitions.text: A child gets attached to this
definitions.meaning: a comfort object such as a blanket or soft toy that a small child clings to
the official term for measures keeping sensitive information under wraps

explanation.surface: A child grows attached to something associated with secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a toddler's comfort item and a cloak of official concealment, so each half of the clue is a separate meaning.

clue.text: Dog, for example, of a kind similar to one of the Pointers

definitions.text: similar to one of the Pointers

parts.note: Sirius, the Dog Star, is an example of a star
like means of the same kind, alike

explanation.surface: A dog is likened to one of the pointer breeds of gundog.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pointers are the two stars of the Plough that point to the Pole Star, not gundogs; 'Dog' is the Dog Star, Sirius.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling one of the Plough's pointer stars is to be like a star in appearance.

definitions.meaning: to border on or touch, as two plots of land do
read as ..., a 'but' being an objection

explanation.surface: Someone meets a raised objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet at an edge is to adjoin, and split in two the word reads as an objection: a 'but'.

clue.text: Arrested old farm worker with stray deer

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer

indicators.note: deer letters wander from their places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old farmhand was held up by a deer that had wandered.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrested in the sense of checked or held back in progress, a synonym.

definitions.note: the genus name stands for the whole group of hairstreak butterflies, hence the plural

indicators.note: the butterfly genus sits inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: There are butterflies loose in the school classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Thecla is a genus of hairstreak butterflies, so the name covers several species.

indicators.note: the letters of met green are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the classroom: someone met a green mix as it emerged.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue's surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergent means arising or coming into view, a direct synonym of coming out.

clue.text: Two bits? That's not much to put on here

definitions.text: Two bits? That's not much to put on here

parts.words: Two bits? That's not much to put on here
parts.note: a two-piece swimsuit, scanty clothing, also named after a Pacific atoll used for tests

explanation.surface: Two small pieces are hardly enough to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: The skimpy two-piece swimsuit is literally two bits, and 'here' hints at the Pacific atoll it is named after.

clue.text: "Night steals across the sky" — an obvious lift

definitions.meaning: read whimsically, nightfall robs the sky of its light
a blatant overcharge or theft done openly, lift meaning steal

explanation.surface: A poetic line about dusk is followed by a remark about a blatant theft.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a flagrant rip-off, and literally the theft of daylight that nightfall commits.

clue.text: To set up stable accommodation is hard

indicators.note: accommodation as adjustment, so the letters of stable are adjusted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Arranging housing for horses is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable accommodation' reads as housing for horses, but 'accommodation' is the anagram signal, reshuffling STABLE into ESTABL; H for hard is pencil-grading shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish something is to found or set it up, a synonym.

definitions.meaning: in Greek thought, a person's allotted fate or portion

explanation.surface: A young woman's fate.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common female name and also the Greek word for fate, one's allotted share.

clue.text: Finally, Utopia turned out to be classless

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order, giving a rearrangement
the closing letter of Utopia is taken

explanation.surface: In the end, a utopia proved to have no social classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' gives A, the end of Utopia; 'out' rearranges A with TURNED. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrated means not ranked or graded, so without a class assigned.

definitions.meaning: a sweet fruit concentrate diluted to drink

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
mug and dial are both slang for the face

explanation.surface: Someone's cup holds a hot beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both friendly and warm in manner and a fruit-based drink.

indicators.note: all but the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian means Irish

explanation.surface: A goddess is nearly all Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this goddess is the messenger of the gods and personifies the rainbow.

indicators.note: the port is placed inside the reworked letters
the letters of boring are operated on and rearranged

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A harbour is enlarged by a drilling operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like a dull adjective, but it is the fodder: 'operation' rearranges it to BROING, and 'in' puts the Yemeni port ADEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadening means widening or expanding, a synonym in the same -ing form.

parts.note: the word means both gave, as in produced a crop, and gave up, as in surrendered

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered by various methods.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers producing (a field gives a harvest) and surrendering, so it fits gave up in two different senses.

clue.text: They're made for creating impressions — false ones!

definitions.text: They're made for creating impressions — false ones!

parts.words: They're made for creating impressions — false ones!
parts.note: dental impressions are taken to make false teeth

explanation.surface: Something exists purely to give misleading impressions.
explanation.definitionFit: False teeth are made from impressions of the mouth, and they are false, so they fit the clue's play.

parts.note: censored material is cut out
post is mail, correspondence

explanation.surface: Where would censored letters go?
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote settlement or station, a kind of place.

parts.note: over means in excess, extra
to bear is to carry or transport

explanation.surface: Making too much leads to extra transport.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbear is to bear too much fruit, that is, to produce excessively.

indicators.note: potential suggests what the letters could become, so they are rearranged

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: The best of Portugal's capacity for tourism.
explanation.definitionFit: To top a rival is to outdo or surpass them, a synonym used as a verb.

clue.text: They improve vision by using longer test

indicators.note: the letters of longer test are used up and rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Glasses make a lengthier eye test easier.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorgnettes are spectacles held on a handle, which help their user see.

indicators.note: a broken sword's letters fall apart and are reassembled

explanation.surface: Fix a sword that has snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to mend it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Get set for the daily grind

definitions.text: Get set for the daily grind

parts.words: Get set for the daily grind
parts.note: a baby's teeth come through so it can grind food, read as a set of teeth

explanation.surface: Prepare for the everyday drudgery of work.
explanation.definitionFit: When a baby cuts its teeth it acquires the set it will chew with daily.

indicators.note: the races sit inside the spectacles

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of glasses
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races

explanation.surface: A man competes in glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: TT races are held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a man's first name, so it stands for 'he'.

definitions.meaning: the Roman god of the sea
the eighth planet orbits beyond Uranus

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise about something beside a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Roman sea god and to the planet adjacent to Uranus.

parts.note: 'in the altogether' means naked, and one bathes naked in this

explanation.surface: Where can one get soaked through?
explanation.definitionFit: A tub for bathing is where one gets wet while in the altogether, that is, naked.

indicators.note: the end is chipped off the word

parts.note: tater is informal for potato

explanation.surface: An art gallery shows a potato with a chip out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is a famous group of London art galleries.

definitions.meaning: the flower of something is its best part

explanation.surface: A kind of bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Elite is both a typewriter type size and the pick or flower of a group.

indicators.note: the letters of the hailer may turn into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker could gain strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthier means in better condition, hence stronger, a comparative synonym.
